clue.text: Metal storage device for data, one held by friend

indicators.note: the friend's word holds the other pieces inside it, as something held by a hand

parts.note: a chum is a friend
ROM is read-only memory, a computer storage device
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A piece of hardware storing data, with one unit kept by a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' signals a container: the friend's word is split open to take the storage device and the one.
explanation.definitionFit: This lustrous element is a hard metal used for plating.

clue.text: Note about game must be accurate

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the note goes round the game

parts.note: te is the seventh note in tonic sol-fa
RU is rugby union, the game

explanation.surface: A musical note concerning a sport has to be correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals a container; 'must be' is a link. Rugby union is the usual crossword game for these two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accurate is correct, faithful to the facts: a synonym.

clue.text: got a gun

annotationWithheld.why: The clue as held is 'got a gun (6)': it has no definition and looks cut short; HAS + TEN or HA + STEN cannot be confirmed without the missing words.

clue.text: Gill, for instance, girl in Gulf, swimming

indicators.note: the girl's word goes inside the reworked letters of the gulf
swimming suggests the letters of Gulf moving about and rearranging

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl swims in the Gulf, perhaps for a measure of liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' scrambles the Gulf and 'in' houses the girl within it. A gill is a small liquid measure, a quarter of a pint, so 'for instance' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A gill is an example of a measured quantity filling a drinking vessel.

clue.text: Rearrange special soiree to accommodate Gran, possibly

indicators.note: to accommodate means one set of letters takes another in, here the soiree's letters housing Gran's
special here means made up specially, so the party's letters are rearranged
possibly signals that Gran's letters may be in another order

explanation.surface: Someone is planning a special evening party so that Granny can come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' scrambles the party and 'possibly' scrambles Gran, and 'to accommodate' puts the second inside the first. The paper printed the French word without its double E.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange something is to put it into a new order: a synonym.

clue.text: Newly sculpted pieta, one in foreign capital

indicators.note: the single letter for one goes inside the newly made arrangement
sculpted anew, so the letters of the statue's name are reshaped

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A freshly carved Pieta, one of them in a city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly sculpted' scrambles the statue's name and 'in' tucks the one inside it. A pieta is a sculpture of Mary holding the dead Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: This Taiwanese city is the seat of government of the island, a capital outside Britain.

clue.text: Retail outlet quick to limit damage

indicators.note: to limit means to enclose and bound, so the speedy word wraps round the hurt

parts.note: pacy means quick
harm means damage

explanation.surface: A shop moves fast to contain the harm done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to limit' reads as reducing harm, but signals a container: the quick word encloses the damage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist's shop is a retailer selling medicines.

clue.text: Certainly, confused type will be seen an affluent professional

parts.note: yup is a casual yes, certainly
pie is printers' jargon for jumbled-up metal type

explanation.surface: Sure enough, a muddled sort will be taken for a wealthy career person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused type' looks like a muddled person but is printers' 'pie', a heap of mixed type. 'will be seen' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A young urban professional earning well, the 1980s label for the moneyed young worker.

clue.text: General introducing method to determine latitude

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the US Civil War
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A general brings in a technique for fixing position north or south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latitude' looks geographical, but here it means freedom of action. 'introducing' and 'to determine' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is room for manoeuvre, freedom to act: a synonym.

clue.text: Nothing like!

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing like!' reads as an exclamation, but it splits into two definitions: tennis zero, and the verb for liking.
explanation.definitionFit: Score of zero in tennis; also a verb for being very fond of something, as in 'I'd adore that'.

clue.text: Caption for pretty pics, maybe?

indicators.note: maybe says the letters of pretty pics might stand in another order

explanation.surface: Someone wants a caption for some attractive photos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges PRETTY PICS; 'for' is a link. A caption is typed text placed under a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A caption is typed text, matter set down on a typewriter rather than by hand.

clue.text: Bishop in colony never backing primate

indicators.note: the bishop's letter is placed inside the colony's abbreviation

parts.note: Gib is short for Gibraltar, a British colony
B is the abbreviation for bishop in chess notation

indicators.note: backing means the word for never is read backwards

parts.note: no can mean never, as in 'no more'

explanation.surface: A bishop in an overseas territory never supports the ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts B into GIB, and 'backing' turns NO into ON. Gibraltar is a British overseas territory at the tip of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-armed ape of south-east Asia is one of the primates.

clue.text: They're at least partly responsible for the kids

definitions.text: They're at least partly responsible for the kids

parts.words: They're at least partly responsible for the kids
parts.note: sounds like fathers of human children, but the kids are young goats and these are the male parents

explanation.surface: Dads share the blame for how the children turn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kids' are young goats, and the fathers are only partly responsible because the nannies do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Male goats father kids, the young of goats.

clue.text: Remarkably daring, if somewhat beneath one?

indicators.note: remarkably suggests the letters behave unusually and end up rearranged

explanation.surface: Bold behaviour that might seem a little below one's dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remarkably' rearranges DARING IF. The answer is Latin shorthand for 'beneath one's dignity'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means unbecoming, below one's dignity: a synonym.

clue.text: Fish from island west of Egypt .

indicators.note: in a down-reading sense of a map, west of means placed to the left, so the island comes first

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides in Scotland
ET is the international vehicle code for Egypt

explanation.surface: A fish caught off an island lying west of Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'west of' puts the island first. Mull is an island off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The grey or red mullet is a food fish.

clue.text: Blackmail case started by former wife

indicators.note: started by means the second piece is placed at the front of the first

parts.note: an ex is a former wife
a case at law is an action

explanation.surface: A blackmail lawsuit was brought by an ex-wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'started by' puts EX ahead of ACTION, a law case.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaction is demanding money by force or threat, extortion such as blackmail.

clue.text: … Fish? Get set to catch one

indicators.note: to catch means holding inside, so the word for set closes round the letter

parts.note: to set something down is to place it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An angler readies to land a single fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' puts I inside PLACE. 'Get' is a link; the ellipsis continues from the fish clue before.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a flatfish caught for food.

clue.text: Time gear changes to move a fair distance?

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the two words alter their order

explanation.surface: Time to change gear, to drive a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges TIME GEAR. The definition is a cryptic hint, with the question mark: to leave one's country is a long move.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country for another, a long relocation.

clue.text: Person constructing enclosures — following drawing, he'll get stuck in

definitions.text: following drawing, he'll get stuck in

explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' sounds like sketching but means drawing a sword, and 'get stuck in' is literal: the swordsman thrusts.
explanation.definitionFit: One putting up barriers round fields; also a swordsman, who after drawing his blade lunges to pierce an opponent.

clue.text: Childhood friend to deliver coup de grace on board?

definitions.text: to deliver coup de grace on board

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as two words: play the final checkmate on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion a child plays with; also, split, to play checkmate, finishing the game on the chessboard.

clue.text: Scrubber in bathroom, fibrous and hard, primarily

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet or bathroom

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the first letter of each of those words is used

explanation.surface: A rough-textured scrubbing sponge in the bathroom, fibrous and tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes F, A, H from 'fibrous and hard'. 'in' is a link. Loo is everyday British for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried gourd skin used as a bath sponge for scrubbing the body.

clue.text: It helps to bring things up

definitions.text: It helps to bring things up

parts.words: It helps to bring things up
parts.note: sounds like raising topics or lifting loads, but the things brought up are a stomach's contents

explanation.surface: Something that aids in raising matters for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring things up' sounds like raising a subject, but it means vomiting.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance taken to make the patient vomit.

clue.text: New emblem under English flag

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below, so the English letter goes above

parts.note: a sign is an emblem or symbol

explanation.surface: A new badge appears below the English banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts N + SIGN below E in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a naval flag or banner.

clue.text: Toys once popular bound to take off again, if you use them

definitions.text: Toys once popular bound to take off again, if you use them

parts.words: Toys once popular bound to take off again, if you use them
parts.note: a 'bound to take off again' reads like a fad returning, but describes jumping springs that leap the user up again

explanation.surface: A craze of the past is sure to come back into fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to take off again' reads as 'certain to become popular again', but describes bouncing: each bound launches the rider back up.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring-loaded sticks children bounce on, a toy craze of earlier decades.

clue.text: Coastal feature in part of Russia moving westwards

indicators.note: in an across clue, moving westwards means read right to left
in part means only a section of the words is used, running across them

explanation.surface: A coastline in a region of Russia shifting west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in part' takes FRUS from 'oF RUSsia', and 'moving westwards' turns it right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: The surf is the foaming waves breaking on a shore.

clue.text: Has to have a drink after financial transaction

indicators.note: after places the drink behind the first piece

parts.note: 's is a contraction of has, as in 'he's got'
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: Someone needs a drink once the deal is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' gives S, as in he's ('he has'), and 'after' puts ALE behind it. 'to have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale is an exchange of goods for money.

clue.text: Engage in handicraft, also producing coloured design

parts.note: to tat is to make tatting, a knotted lace handicraft
too means also

explanation.surface: Doing a craft also yields a colourful pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: TAT means to make tatting, a knotted lace. 'producing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ink pattern pricked into the skin, often in colour.

clue.text: Control speed when going around, say, centre of Hull

indicators.note: going around means the speed's word encircles the other pieces

parts.note: rate means speed
eg (for example) is a way of saying 'say'

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letters of the word Hull

explanation.surface: Keeping an eye on speed when travelling round the middle of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link; 'going around' signals that the speed word encloses the example abbreviation and the core of the city's name. Hull is an English port city.
explanation.definitionFit: To regulate is to govern or manage: a synonym.
